answer: Root each identity in a hardware enclave: the agent submits a signed TEE attestation whose per-device key is sealed tight as a walnut and cannot be forged off that chip. The protocol fences every distinct enclave as its own meadow that earns its own reward, while all identities presenting the same enclave measurement are herded into a single haven and must split one share. A sybil fleet behind one machine collapses to a single haven-share, so faking N identities costs N genuinely separate attestation-capable devices: linear hardware per clone, not one chip wearing a thousand masks.
